justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are addressed: Catalog & Search handles search, Order & Checkout coordinates purchases, Content & Review manages ratings, and Recommendation provides suggestions. Cart state persistence is slightly implicit within Order & Checkout.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Scalability and sub-2s latency targets are supported via Amazon CloudFront, OpenSearch, ElastiCache Redis caching in Localization & Tax, and asynchronous decoupled processing via Amazon SQS and EventBridge.
justifications.compatibility: External integrations are explicitly specified with defined protocols: Payment Gateway and Third-Party Shipping Provider via HTTPS, and Tax & Currency Provider via Localization & Tax supporting USD, EUR, and GBP.
justifications.usability: Dedicated interfaces address all personas: Shoppers use Frontend Container with Radix UI and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, while Store Administrators and Support use Admin UI within Admin Back-Office.
justifications.reliability: Reliability is supported by Resilience4j in TaxCalculationEngine, Idempotency Manager, and SQS DLQs. However, multi-region failover and data replication mechanisms across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 are not detailed.
justifications.security: Strong security mechanisms are included: Perimeter Router and Security Enforcement with JWT validation, Auth & RBAC Controller, Audit Logger with S3 Object Lock, and Compliance & Consent Manager for GDPR/CCPA.
justifications.maintainability: Services are well-decomposed around business domains using gRPC and event-driven patterns. However, Content & Review component definitions conflate external infrastructure and actors with internal components.
justifications.portability: The design relies heavily on AWS-managed services like Amazon DocumentDB, OpenSearch, Comprehend, and S3 Object Lock without abstraction layers, limiting portability beyond AWS.

PERF-01.justification: Edge caching via CloudFront and OpenSearch indexing handle high read loads, though heavy client-side React SPA bundles may challenge 2s load times on 3G.
tradeoffs: Client-side SPA bundle richness versus initial load latency on cellular networks

PERF-02.justification: Recommendation recomputation occurs asynchronously via offline batch jobs in ECS/SageMaker, persisting pre-computed results to Redis without impacting online browsing traffic.
sensitivity_points: Redis memory bandwidth and write throughput during batch ingestion
tradeoffs: Serving stale pre-computed recommendations versus online runtime processing overhead

AVAIL-01.justification: SQS/SNS event publishing decouples fulfillment so orders can complete, but synchronous shipping rate calculation during checkout lacks an explicit fallback mechanism in the design.
sensitivity_points: Asynchronous message delivery reliability in SQS
tradeoffs: Immediate shipping confirmation accuracy versus checkout resilience during third-party outages

AVAIL-02.justification: Target regions are defined, but the architecture lacks explicit cross-region data replication (e.g. Aurora Global Database) and automated multi-region failover routing to guarantee zero lost orders.
sensitivity_points: Health check detection latency for regional failover
tradeoffs: Strict cross-region data consistency versus write latency during checkout

MOD-01.justification: Currency handling is centralized in Localization & Tax and dynamic conversion caching exists, but Frontend's Localization & Currency Context explicitly hardcodes USD, EUR, and GBP state.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between frontend state components and allowed ISO currency lists
tradeoffs: Static client currency types versus dynamic currency configuration loading

MOD-02.justification: The Algorithm Engine runs offline batch jobs isolated from other services, writing to a Redis data store. Changing the algorithm requires no modifications outside the Recommendation container.
sensitivity_points: Schema compatibility of co-purchase matrices written to the cache
tradeoffs: Batch algorithm simplicity versus real-time model training adaptability

SEC-01.justification: The API Gateway has perimeter routing and logging, but critical OWASP mitigations like AWS WAF, request validation layers, and input sanitization mechanisms are omitted from the design.
sensitivity_points: WAF rule coverage at the edge
Input validation rigor across polyglot microservice controllers
tradeoffs: Edge-level payload deep inspection latency versus backend sanitization complexity

SEC-02.justification: Beyond a client-side cookie banner, the architecture lacks mechanisms, services, or workflows to orchestrate, execute, or verify personal data erasure across multiple databases and audit logs.
sensitivity_points: Tracking personal data across polyglot databases
Conflict with immutable WORM audit storage
tradeoffs: Tamper-proof compliance logging versus legal right-to-erasure requirements
